title: paged KV cache: adaptive block allocator + reuse & pinning optimizations
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: This PR improves the paged KV cache block allocator and block manager by introducing an adaptive reuse heuristic and stronger locality-aware pinning. Motivation: high eviction churn and suboptimal locality under mixed workloads were causing unnecessary GPU memory traffic and tail-latency spikes on long-context serving. This change reduces allocator fragmentation, increases KV cache hit stability, and reduces tail latency for long-running chat sessions. Key changes: 1) split the allocator free lists by locality (same-device, peer-device) to favor reuse of nearby blocks; 2) introduce pinned reference counts and a lightweight pinning API so hot KV pages can be preferentially kept in GPU memory; 3) adaptive reuse heuristic that biases allocation toward recently used block classes and periodically demotes cold classes to TTL-based eviction; 4) compacting fast-path for small contiguous allocations to reduce fragmentation; 5) better metrics and tracing hooks for block lifecycle (alloc/free/pin/unpin/evict) and a new benchmark harness for simulating mixed chat+inference traffic. The description below includes a short checklist of work done and validation: - [x] allocator free-list split and locality accounting - [x] pinned block reference counts and API - [x] adaptive reuse heuristic + config knobs - [x] unit + integration tests for allocator invariants - [x] perf canary + benchmark results (see ci checks) - [x] docs and config examples for tuning pin TTL and reuse thresholds Backwards compatibility: allocator changes are internal to the paged-kv subsystem and are guarded behind a feature flag (kv.paged.adaptive_reuse=true) so operators can roll out progressively. No public API changes to Redwood API are included.
commits: refactor(kv): split allocator free lists by locality and add accounting
feat(kv): add pinned block reference counts and pin/unpin API
perf(kv): adaptive reuse heuristic with configurable thresholds
perf(kv): compacting allocation fast-path for small contiguous requests
test(kv): allocator invariants and stress tests
ci: add perf canary job and benchmark harness
docs: add tuning guide for KV pinning and reuse
review_comments: Marco Liu: Please add invariants to ensure pinned blocks are not reclaimed by the TTL path - addressed in second commit (added pinned reference count and checks).

Evan Brooks: Can we expose the adaptive threshold as a runtime-config flag? We should avoid a forced rollout. Reply: added kv.paged.adaptive_reuse flag and three tuning knobs (hot_bias, cold_threshold, demote_interval).
Sasha Martinez: Benchmarks look promising - can you add a long-tail latency CDF? Reply: added bench + perf-canary scenario and uploaded aggregated canary results to the PR pipeline artifacts.
Reviewer (CI): initial integration tests failed due to a race in the compacting fast-path. Fix: added atomic handoff and retry path in allocator (commit 4).
Marco Liu: approved after small nits; requested changelog entry - added to docs/ops/kv_cache_tuning.md
ci_checks: perf-canary: pass (8-12% throughput improvement on mixed chat workload, 15% tail-latency reduction at 99th percentile)
release_notes: Adaptive reuse and locality-aware pinning for paged KV cache: reduces eviction churn, improves throughput (8-12%) and 99th percentile tail latency (~15%) on mixed chat+inference workloads. Configurable via kv.paged.adaptive_reuse and tuning knobs in docs/ops/kv_cache_tuning.md.
